overview: Tunisia's femtech scene is small but distinctive, anchored by Feel by Luna, an AI symptom tool for endometriosis and reproductive health that lets women describe symptoms by voice in French, Arabic or Tunisian dialect, and one of eleven startups in UNICEF's first Femtech Ventures cohort. The country pairs a long-standing, progressive reproductive-health legal framework (contraception legal since 1961, abortion since 1973, free family planning) with a maturing startup infrastructure, the Startup Act, Smart Capital and the ANAVA fund of funds, plus established IVF clinics dating to the late 1980s. Overall venture funding is thin, with near-zero disclosed equity deals in H1 2026, so dedicated women's health capital remains scarce and largely donor or blended.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: The headline development is a Tunisian femtech startup breaking into a flagship global women's health platform, alongside a national push into AI e-health.

items.text: Feel by Luna, a Tunisian AI e-health tool for endometriosis and reproductive symptoms, selected for UNICEF Femtech Ventures first cohort with up to USD 100,000 equity-free plus a year of technical support.
Local coverage profiles Feel by Luna as tackling endometriosis, which affects roughly one in ten women and takes 7 to 10 years to diagnose, with voice input in French, Arabic and Tunisian dialect.
President Kais Saied and Health Minister Mustapha Ferjani announce Tunisia's first fully digital hospital, with AI diagnostics and telemedicine to cut urban-rural care gaps.
Tunisian startups raise just USD 300,000 in H1 2026 with no disclosed equity rounds, a sharp contrast with Morocco, underscoring how thin capital is for all sectors including femtech.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Tunisia has one of the region's most progressive reproductive-health legal frameworks, now paired with a national e-health and AI agenda.

items.text: Contraception legalized; free access to contraception, abortion and counseling later ensured through the national family planning program, with free prenatal and postnatal consultations.
Health and ICT ministers agree to build the national health information system, launch an AI system to improve care quality, and prepare a digital hospital for inland regions.
UNFPA launches its 2025 to 2030 Start with Her strategy for reproductive, maternal and newborn health, framing Tunisia's continued reproductive-health support.
Startup Act label and pre-label application session held, the labeling regime that gives qualifying health and femtech startups fiscal and operational benefits.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Support infrastructure exists via the Startup Act, accelerators and a healthtech-specific structure, even as dedicated women's-health programming is limited.

items.text: Feel by Luna joins UNICEF Femtech Ventures, a five-year (2025 to 2030) catalytic platform backed by Sweden and Temasek Foundation, giving Tunisia a seat in a global femtech pipeline.
Connect'Innov operates as a Tunisia-based support structure dedicated to detecting and promoting HealthTech innovation, notably e-health, medtech and biotech.
Flat6Labs Tunis runs the Anava Seed Fund and has helped 20+ of the 210+ Startup Act labeled companies, providing the accelerator layer femtech founders can tap.
Women-led Tunisian startups have grown from local roots to global reach, part of a wider push (documented by Hivos) to back female founders in the ecosystem.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Femtech-specific capital in Tunisia is dominated by grants and blended funds rather than private equity rounds, reflecting a broadly capital-starved market.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: The map spans one flagship femtech startup, established IVF clinics, national e-health bodies and startup infrastructure.

items.name: Feel by Luna
items.note: AI e-health tool for endometriosis and reproductive symptoms; voice input in French, Arabic and Tunisian dialect; UNICEF Femtech Ventures cohort 1

items.name: FERTILLIA (La Rose Clinique)
items.note: Assisted reproduction center; described as the first Tunisian institution entirely devoted to reproductive medicine (since 1988)

items.name: EVE Fertility Center
items.note: Medically assisted reproduction center in Tunisia offering IVF and related services

items.name: Hannibal International Clinic
items.note: Tunis private clinic (inaugurated 2012) accredited by the Ministry of Public Health, offering IVF and maternal services

items.name: Connect'Innov
items.note: Tunisia-based support structure dedicated to HealthTech innovation (e-health, medtech, biotech)

items.name: Flat6Labs Tunis
items.note: Seed accelerator managing the Anava Seed Fund; backs Startup Act labeled companies

items.name: Smart Capital
items.note: Operator of Startup Tunisia and the Startup Act label; steward of the ANAVA fund of funds

items.name: ONFP (Office National de la Famille et de la Population)
items.note: National body delivering Tunisia's free family-planning and reproductive-health services

items.name: Tunisia Digital / Virtual Hospital initiative
items.note: National e-health program building the first fully digital hospital with AI diagnostics and telemedicine to reach inland regions

items.name: UNFPA Tunisia
items.note: Active since 1974; extends reproductive and maternal health services, especially in remote rural areas

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Femtech-relevant capital comes mainly from donor-backed platforms, blended funds of funds and regional gender-lens investors rather than pure private VC.

items.name: UNICEF Femtech Ventures
items.role: Equity-free capital (up to USD 100K) plus technical support to Feel by Luna

items.name: Government of Sweden
items.role: Founding backer of UNICEF Femtech Ventures supporting the Tunisian cohort startup

items.name: Temasek Foundation
items.role: Founding backer of UNICEF Femtech Ventures

items.name: ANAVA Fund of Funds
items.role: EUR 200M target fund of funds (World Bank, CDC, KfW backed) seeding VC funds that can finance health startups

items.name: Flat6Labs (Anava Seed Fund)
items.role: Seed accelerator investor across Tunisian innovation startups

items.name: AfricInvest
